newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen rise on short-covering, gains capped.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen rise on short-covering, gains capped.

text.p: Short-covering lifted SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures on Tuesday, but dealers said further gains would be slow ahead of the release of the Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s tankan survey.
"Sentiment is firm going into the tankan. Recent data has shown weaknesses in the economy," a trader at a U.S. house said.

Dealers said the BOJ's quarterly business sentiment survey was expected to present a negative picture, confirming growing market confidence that the central bank would leave interest rates steady for the foreseeable future.
December Euroyen stood at 99.11 at 1115 GMT after hitting a high of 99.14 against its IMM close at 99.09. March, which saw higher turnover, was at 98.90 against a high of 98.94.
Dealers said March could become the lead contract in the next day or two following June's expiry on Monday.
A dealer at a Japanese brokerage said December Euroyen could drift back down to 99.05/06 if it failed to climb above the 99.15 level.
"If it breaks above 99.15, it will quickly push up to 99.23/25 because those who shorted may turn around and go long there," he added.
September JGBs ended at 124.24 against a previous 123.94.
Eurodollar futures ended little changed ahead of the release of the U.S. May Consumer Price Index (CPI), due at 1230 GMT.
Economists polled by Reuters expect the CPI to be up by 0.2 percent in May after a 0.1 percent rise in April.
The most actively traded September contract ended at 94.145 against its IMM close at 94.150.
